_comment: CURATED SPECIMEN (BL-123, decision D-10 option A). Copied from the producer's own example translations with ONE field changed: `decisions`. Everything else is the producer's, so the section stays consistent with the store it was rendered from. THE CURATION RULE, applied identically to every section: a board ask stays only where a DATE or a BREACHED THRESHOLD forces it this quarter. Everything else the CISO speaks to. Asks were DROPPED, never re-pitched from board to management to get under the number — assemble_pack.py:485 names that failure and it would be the dishonest way to hit five. ——— THIS SECTION: M-001's fund-or-accept dropped: a service level is not the appetite band, and nothing dates it to this quarter. The metric still reports; the CISO speaks to it. The management restore-test item stays because it is management work, not a board ask.
executiveSummary: Six numbers are tracked; three are past the line we set for them and two of those are still moving the wrong way. The pattern is not random. Patching and phishing both worsened this quarter, and they are the two halves of the same route in — a message that gets clicked and a machine that has not been fixed. Identity moved the other way and is now effectively complete, and attacker dwell time is down by three days, so the detection investment is showing. The one that should concern the board most is not the worst number but the oldest: we last tested a backup restore in November, at 40% success, and have not measured it since. That is eight months without evidence on the control that decides whether an incident is a bad week or a business-continuity failure. We are asking for two decisions: fund the patching backlog, and schedule a restore test before the next review.

metrics.M-006: We last tested backup restores in November, when 40% succeeded, and we have not measured since — eight months without evidence on the control that decides whether a ransomware incident is recoverable. This is a gap in what we know, not a claim that recovery has failed.
metrics.M-001: Critical patches applied inside our own service level fell from 93% to 88%, crossing the 90% line the board agreed. The gap is concentrated in internet-facing systems, which is the population where the number matters most.
metrics.M-003: Simulated phishing click rate rose from 4.1% to 6.8%, past our 6% warning line. Combined with the patching slip above, this is the same attack path getting easier at both ends.
metrics.M-002: Median attacker dwell time came down from 11 days to 8. The detection work is producing the effect it was funded for, and this is the clearest return in the set.
metrics.M-004: Privileged accounts covered by multi-factor authentication reached 99%, up from 96%. The remaining accounts are service accounts with a documented plan, not oversights.
metrics.M-005: We blocked 2.14 million malicious emails this quarter. This is a volume figure, not a risk figure — it measures how much arrived, not how much got through, and it should not be read as reassurance.

decisions.text: Schedule and resource a backup restore test before the next review, so M-006 reports a measured figure rather than an eight-month-old one.
